newsitem.title: USA: L.A. council gives initial go-ahead for arena plan.
newsitem.headline: L.A. council gives initial go-ahead for arena plan.

text.p: The Los Angeles City Council agreed on Wednesday to pursue a proposed $200-million-plus sports and entertainment arena for the Los Angeles Kings hockey team and basketball's Lakers.
The council voted 11-to-1 to pursue the project.
With the vote, negotiators for the city and the L.A. Arena Company LLC said they would begin to draft a memorandum of understanding. The memorandum should be completed by Oct 15.
If that document was approved by the city council, the agreement would be binding pending environmental and other reviews, said John Semcken of the L.A. Arena Co.
The arena itself is projected to cost about $200 million and will be privately funded.

But Los Angeles would issue municipal bonds to fund the acquisition of land and fund infrastructure improvements. Under the current proposal, the city would provide up to $70.5 million in bond proceeds for the project.
The total project cost would be up to $280 million, Semcken said.
